chunks: Al-Kafi: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Khashshab, from Ghiyath ibn Kalub, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

that two men disputed in front of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) regarding an animal … it was said to him: what if it is not in the possession of either one of them, but both produce evidence? He said: I make them both swear an oath, and whichever one swears and the other reneges, I award it to the one who swore; if both of them swear, I award it to them as two halves …

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali rule on a dispute over property when both parties claim ownership and neither has possession?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (AS) establishes the principle of *Yamin* (oath) in civil disputes where possession is absent, reflecting the practical application of justice in early Islamic courts. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the weight of the oath as a decisive evidentiary tool, particularly when the defendant refuses to swear, thereby validating the claimant's assertion. This mechanism underscores the balance between legal certainty and fairness in resolving property conflicts without requiring complex forensic evidence.

en.ammaar-muslim: 3. [3/-] al-Kafi: Muhammad b. Yahya from Muhammad b. Ahmad from al-Khashshab from Ghiyath b. Kalub from Ishaq b. Ammar from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام that:

two men disputed with each other in front of the commander of the faithful عليه السلام about an animal (each one laid a claim to it) … it was said to him: what if it is not in the hands of either one of them [no one has possession of it] but both produce evidence [have witnesses for it]? he said: I make them both to swear an oath and I rule in favour of the one who swears and against the one who reneges, but if both of them swear I rule for each of them to have one-half of it …
